decks.notes: The deck is focused on assembling and resolving the combo of Doomsday with Thassa's Oracle to win the game by eliminating the opponent's entire library. The deck includes powerful cards like Black Lotus, Force of Will, and Necropotence to support the combo and protect it from disruption. It also includes card selection and card draw spells like Ponder, Brainstorm, and Dig Through Time to find the combo pieces quickly. Overall, the deck aims to quickly assemble the combo and win the game in a few turns.

This deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's game plan with hatebears like Anointed Peacekeeper, Archon of Emeria, and Thalia, Guardian of Thraben, while also applying pressure with aggressive creatures like Seasoned Dungeoneer and White Plume Adventurer. By utilizing cards like Cavern of Souls and Chancellor of the Annex, it aims to protect its creatures from countermagic and disrupt the opponent's spells. The deck also includes powerful artifacts like Black Lotus and Moxen for fast mana acceleration, along with disruptive spells like Trinisphere and Swords to Plowshares for added control.

This Dimir Control deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan through counterspells like Force of Will and Spell Pierce, as well as removal spells like Fatal Push. It also utilizes card advantage with Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time to pull ahead in resources. The deck also has the ability to recur key cards with Lurrus of the Dream-Den and can generate additional value with Mishra's Bauble and Psychic Frog. With a mix of disruption, card advantage, and recursion, this deck aims to control the flow of the game and outvalue the opponent.

The main concept of this deck is to overwhelm the opponent with aggressive artifact creatures and disrupt their game plan with disruptive artifacts like Trinisphere, Null Rod, and Chalice of the Void. The deck aims to control the game by utilizing Mishra's Workshop and other mana acceleration artifacts to play threats like Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Stonecoil Serpent quickly. It also has cards like Crucible of Worlds and Ghost Quarter to disrupt the opponent's mana base. The deck is focused on establishing early board presence and controlling the game with disruptive artifacts in order to win quickly.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy with counterspells like Spell Pierce, Force of Will, and Force of Negation while controlling the board with removal spells like Fatal Push and Wasteland. It relies on card advantage through cards like Lórien Revealed, Treasure Cruise, and Dig Through Time to outvalue the opponent. It also uses cards like Psychic Frog and Nihil Spellbomb to disrupt the opponent's graveyard strategies. The deck utilizes a restricted vintage card pool to create a powerful and resourceful control deck.

The deck focuses on playing disruptive creatures like Anointed Peacekeeper and Archon of Emeria while using hate cards like Chancellor of the Annex and Trinisphere to slow down the opponent. It also includes efficient mana sources and disruptive artifacts to outpace the opponent and disrupt their game plan. The goal is to establish a aggressive board presence while preventing the opponent from executing their strategy effectively, ultimately overwhelming them with a combination of aggressive creatures and disruptive elements.

The deck utilizes the Oath of Druids combo to cheat out powerful creatures like Atraxa, Grand Unifier and Narset, Parter of Veils early in the game. It also includes a variety of counterspells like Force of Will and Force of Negation to control the opponent's plays. The deck has a solid card draw engine with Ancestral Recall, Dig Through Time, and Preordain. Show and Tell is included as an alternate way to get big threats onto the battlefield. Overall, the deck aims to control the game and overwhelm the opponent with powerful creatures.

The deck focuses on generating mana quickly with powerful artifacts like Mana Vault, Mana Crypt, and the Moxen, while also using card draw and manipulation spells like Sensei's Divining Top and Brainstorm. The key strategy is to set up a big turn where you can play Paradoxical Outcome to bounce your artifacts back to hand and draw a huge number of cards, generating even more mana and resources to win the game in one explosive turn. The deck is designed to be efficient and consistent in executing this combo strategy.

The deck focuses on utilizing artifacts to generate mana and disrupt opponents, while also utilizing aggressive creatures to apply pressure. It aims to control the board with cards like Wasteland and Crucible of Worlds, while also utilizing powerful artifacts like Golos, Tireless Pilgrim and Nettlecyst to establish a strong board presence. Cards like Null Rod and Sphere of Resistance are used to disrupt opponents' strategies, while cards like Stonecoil Serpent and Lodestone Golem are used for quick and efficient damage output. The deck aims to quickly overwhelm opponents with a combination of disruptive artifacts and aggressive creatures.

This deck focuses on assembling the Doomsday combo to win the game quickly. It utilizes cards like Demonic Tutor, Vampiric Tutor, and Dig Through Time to find necessary combo pieces such as Doomsday and Thassa's Oracle. The deck also includes cards like Force of Will, Flusterstorm, and Mental Misstep to protect the combo. Additionally, the deck includes various cantrips like Preordain and Ponder to dig through the deck efficiently. With the right cards in hand, the deck aims to cast Doomsday, set up the perfect pile, and win the game with Thassa's Oracle.
